subject: [Escalation] Inflight retry churn causing p99 regressions & 429s
messages:
From: Sam Torres <sam.torres@acmeapp.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 20 Apr 2027 09:12:27 -0700
Subject: Re: Customer alert: p99 latency jump and 429s

Marcus —

We started seeing a big regression around 08:45 PT. P95 moved from ~120ms to ~1.1s and p99 is spiking above 5s; we're also observing a wave of 429s and timeouts downstream. Our client UX is timing out and customers are filing tickets.

I attached a short screenshot and a few sampled requests for your team to look at (latency-dash.png, sample-requests.log).

Two notes from our side:
- We do have aggressive client-side retries enabled (exponential backoff) and it looks like a burst of retries started at ~08:47 which correlates with the earliest 5xx/429s in our logs.
- This is production traffic across multiple regions but impact looks concentrated on us-west-2 endpoints.

Can you advise next steps and ETA? This is impacting our SLOs.

— Sam
Infra/Integrations — Acme App

From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
To: Sam Torres <sam.torres@acmeapp.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
Cc: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 20 Apr 2027 10:15:49 -07:00
Subject: Re: Customer alert: p99 latency jump and 429s

Sam / Marcus —

Triage notes (first pass):
- Correlated our API gateway logs with Acme's sample requests. We see a sharp rise in 429 responses starting at 08:46 PT. Many of Acme's client retries are arriving within 100–300ms windows and appear to be driving sustained queue pressure on the hosted pool.
- The affected model routes are: open-gpt-3.8-large and gpt-3.8-reranker (hosted-us-west).
- No recent rollout on our side in the last 24 hours; kernel/quant config unchanged.

Immediate mitigation options (choices):
- Apply a short-lived adaptive backoff policy (server-side) to the Acme API key to reduce retry amplification (recommended for now).
- Temporarily route Acme traffic to a higher-capacity dedicated pool (longer but safer).
- Ask Acme to throttle their client retry settings while we stabilize (fastest but requires their coordination).

Requesting permission to apply server-side adaptive backoff for 30 minutes while we observe impact. This would essentially smooth retry bursts by rejecting repetitive retries more deterministically and allow queue depth to recover (we would monitor p95/p99 and 429 rate).

Attachments: latency-dash.png (screenshot), sample-requests.log (snippets).

— Monica
Account Exec — Redwood Inference
From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
Cc: Sam Torres <sam.torres@acmeapp.com>
Date: Tue, 20 Apr 2027 11:40:02 -07:00
Subject: Re: Customer alert: p99 latency jump and 429s

Update from SRE (initial debugging):
- Root cause hypothesis: retry storm amplification. We see a feedback loop where early 429s from queue saturation trigger client retries, which then increase concurrency and pushing more requests into the hot path causing higher latencies and additional 429s.
- Traces show lock contention on the KV cache path under sustained small-batch traffic and a growing queue size on the host serving process.
- Mitigation executed: applied server-side adaptive backoff for Acme API key (10s window, deterministic reject for repeat requests beyond 3 retries). Immediate effect: 60% drop in 429s and p95 reduced from ~1.1s to ~420ms within 7 minutes. p99 still elevated (~1.8s) — working on reducing tail.

Next steps:
1) Keep adaptive backoff for 30 minutes and monitor.
2) Warm up an overflow dedicated pool and test routing if tail doesn't improve within 45 minutes.
3) Work with Acme to adjust client retry jitter/upper bound to flatten bursts.

I'll open DP-7843 and attach traces; pinging Laura for visibility and exec escalation if we need to expedite capacity.

— Hannah
Senior SRE — Redwood Inference
From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
To: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>, Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.ai>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>, Sam Torres <sam.torres@acmeapp.com>
Date: Tue, 20 Apr 2027 16:05:03 -07:00
Subject: Exec summary and ask: Acme outage risk due to retry churn (p99 regressions)

Laura / Sean —

Summary: Acme (large integration) experienced a sudden p95/p99 latency regression and elevated 429 rate starting 08:45 PT today. Immediate cause appears to be a retry amplification loop: initial 429s from transient queue pressure triggered dense client retries, which increased load and elongated tail latencies. Hannah applied a server-side adaptive backoff that reduced 429s by ~60% and improved p95, but p99 remains above acceptable thresholds.

Customer impact: Acme is seeing degraded product experience and increased support tickets; this has potential renewal risk if not fully mitigated within 24–48 hours.

Requested exec support:
- Approve warm-up and short-term routing of Acme traffic to a dedicated overflow pool (~2–4 GPUs) while we stabilize (estimate 45–90 minutes to provision and test). This is a temporary capacity call; cost will be charged to contingency.
- If approved, accelerate capacity provisioning (SRE/infra will require approved sign-off).
- Authorize a goodwill credit discussion if impact extends beyond 24 hours (Monica can manage with customer).

Current mitigation status: adaptive backoff in place; SRE monitoring. DP-7843 created and linked here: https://jira.redwood.ai/browse/DP-7843.

I'll stand by for go-ahead.

Thanks,
Marcus
Senior Sales Engineer — Redwood Inference
